text:
jordan-pm: Heads-up — AcmeHealth requested a pilot that recommends batching, caching, and quantization profiles per route plus eval-triggered alerts. They insist we do not change their model weights. p99 target ~150ms; target ~30% token cost reduction. Can we outline a minimal safe scope?
maya-eng: yes in principle. question: do we ship "advice only" or allow auto-apply for canaries?
simon-ml: I'd push "advice only" initially. Recommender can output batch_size, quant_level, cache_ttl and an expected impact curve. Auto-apply requires stronger gating & legal signoff.
linh-ux: UX: keep it lean. a card showing Suggested Profile + Expected Impact + Confidence. one-click "Apply to Canary" for pilot customers, but default to manual apply.
ara-ops: ops constraints: every change must have a fallback to baseline and an automated rollback path. Log audit events for all applied suggestions. add tenant-level kill-switch.
carl-cs: AcmeHealth emphasized eval-triggered alerts; they want immediate notification if quality degrades on a golden prompt set. how often do we run evals?
simon-ml: proposal: nightly batch eval on the customer golden set + a smoke check post-rollout sampling 100 requests for concordance. Alert if quality delta >3% (F1/ROUGE depending) or semantic drift >5%.
jordan-pm: launch criteria draft: 1) Recommender produces sim-backed delta on staging (latency, tokens) 2) Canary apply to 5% traffic with automatic rollback on eval failure 3) UI to present recommendation + audit trail 4) Ops runbook + SLOs documented
maya-eng: engineering notes: need telemetry hooks for per-route latency histogram, token counts, and cache hit ratio. Batching suggestion requires sequence length distribution histograms to estimate latency vs cost trade-offs.
linh-ux: pilot UI fields: Suggested profile (batch_size, quant_level, cache_ttl), Expected impact (tokens saved %, p99 delta ms), Confidence score, Rationale bullet points, and "Apply to Canary" button. Provide an "Explain" modal with simulation numbers.
ara-ops: security: ensure KMS keys are never emitted in logs. telemetry must be scoped per-tenant. auto-runs TTL and a hard disable flag per tenant.
carl-cs: docs: prepare a one-pager describing what changes when you accept a recommendation and how rollback works. AcmeHealth asked for SLA around rollbacks.
simon-ml: ballpark dev estimate: offline sim harness (2.5w), recommender engine + decisioning (2w), telemetry + integration (2w), canary plumbing + rollback (1w), UI + docs (1w) = ~8.5 weeks. can compress with parallel work.
jordan-pm: tradeoffs: fully automated application reduces friction but increases risk. For pilot, default to suggested + one-click canary. measure customer impact before any auto-apply path.
maya-eng: risks: quantization can shift output distribution subtly — must gate on concordance metrics. batching may increase p99 if we wait for batch fullness; present latency contours. tokenization edge cases can skew sim estimates; include guardrail tests.
linh-ux: can we ship a prototype mock this week to validate wording with AcmeHealth? small clickable mock with fake recommendations will surface acceptance criteria.
simon-ml: will produce sample recommendations from sim harness and a mock API endpoint for the UI.
ara-ops: nightly eval cadence acceptable to start. we'll monitor and tighten cadence if customers need it.
carl-cs: customer wants weekly digest emails with recommendations and applied changes; add opt-in to MVP.
jordan-pm: acceptance for pilot: AcmeHealth sees >=15% token cost reduction in 4 weeks with no >3% quality regression on their golden prompts. MVP should include weekly digest opt-in, canary apply button, and audit trail.
maya-eng: next steps and owners: 1) sim harness PR — simon-ml 2) telemetry schema + ingest plan — maya-eng 3) mock UI — linh-ux 4) ops runbook draft — ara-ops 5) customer docs one-pager — carl-cs
simon-ml: creating branch now and will tag deploy-bot when canary plumbing is ready.
deploy-bot: Canary checklist created: traffic split config, rollback hook, alerting thresholds. Runbook: https://internal/runbooks/opt-recs-canary
jordan-pm: great. I'll confirm acceptance metrics and collect AcmeHealth golden prompts. Sync next Tue. :thumbsup:
